title: Report exports — team review
intro: Help define the export requirements. Answer a question or suggest a change.
notice: Example only. Names are self-entered. Completed means answered, not implemented.

setup.outcome: Decide the scope of the first report download.
setup.readers: Alex supplies monthly comparison examples. Jordan explains access rules. Both know the reporting workflow; neither needs code details.
setup.response_budget: A short choice with one example when needed. Not sure and Someone else should answer are valid replies.
setup.reviewer: Reviewing agent; questionnaire owner resumes manual review if delivery fails.
setup.decision_maker: Questionnaire owner resolves scope conflicts after checking the evidence.
setup.escalation: If evidence conflicts, present both claims to the owner. No response deadline or reminder permission is agreed.

requirements.title: Download a report
requirements.text: Readers need a downloadable report they can share with colleagues.
requirements.details: Keep the first version focused on one report. Access rules must also apply to downloads.

questions.title: Which export format?
questions.prompt: Alex, is CSV sufficient for the monthly comparison?

request.recommendation: Start with CSV; confirm before settling scope.
request.why: A formatted document adds scope to the first version.
request.response: Reply Yes, No, Not sure, or Someone else should answer. If No, give one example CSV cannot support and link a sample if available.

attention.next_action: Alex can confirm CSV or provide an example that needs another format.

questions.title: Who may download?
questions.prompt: Jordan, should download access match the report's viewing permissions?

request.recommendation: Use the same access rules as report viewing.
request.why: Downloaded reports can be shared outside the application.
request.response: Reply Yes, No, Not sure, or Someone else should answer. If No, name the exception and link the policy that requires it.

attention.next_action: Jordan can confirm the access rule or identify the policy owner.

requirements.title: Find previous exports
requirements.text: Readers may need to retrieve a previous export without generating it again.
requirements.details: Retention is still a question, not a delivery commitment.

questions.title: How long should exports remain?
questions.prompt: Which recurring task needs an old export, and how old is it?

request.recommendation: Defer retained downloads until a recurring need is established.
request.why: Retention affects storage and access policy.
request.response: Give one recurring task and the oldest export it needs, or say Not sure. Link a policy if one applies.

attention.next_action: The questionnaire owner needs to identify a respondent who uses previous exports.
